You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I tracked the items by their initial names (e.g., "Black ball") rather than strictly tracking the object currently held by the target person (Eve) through each swap. This led to a confusion in Step 4 where I incorrectly assigned the "Black ball" to Eve instead of the "White present" she actually received from Dave. Next time, I will adopt a "target-focused" strategy: I will ignore the full state of all players and only track the specific object held by Eve. I will start with Eve's initial item (Orange ball) and update it only when Eve is explicitly mentioned in a swap. If Eve swaps with someone, I will replace her current item with the item that person is holding at that specific moment, which I must have tracked or deduced. If Eve is not involved in a swap, her item remains unchanged. This minimizes the cognitive load and reduces the chance of misattributing items between non-target players.

New plan: My previous attempt failed because I attempted to track the full state of all five players simultaneously, which introduced a critical error in Step 4 where I misidentified the item Alice was holding (confusing the "Black ball" with the "White present"). To prevent this, I will switch to a "Target-Only" tracking strategy. I will ignore the items held by Alice, Bob, Claire, and Dave unless they are directly swapping with Eve. I will maintain a single variable for Eve's current item, starting with the "orange ball". I will only update this variable when a swap involving Eve occurs. For those specific steps, I will perform a quick, isolated check of the *other* person's item at that exact moment (e.g., in Step 2, checking what Dave has; in Step 4, checking what Alice has) without maintaining a full history of everyone else. This minimizes the cognitive load and eliminates the risk of cross-contamination between non-target players' items.
